published_statement: v1 p.4, verbatim from the text layer: '|Psi> = 1/sqrt(1+eps^2) (|0> + eps|2>), (2.15) where |0> is the vacuum state satisfying a|0> = 0, and |2> = (1/sqrt2)(a+)^2|0> is the two particle state. Here we take eps, the relative amplitude of the two states, to be real for simplicity. For this state, <:T_ab(x):> = <Psi|:T_ab(x):|Psi> = eps/(1+eps^2) { sqrt2 (T_ab[f_k,f_k] + T_ab[f*_k,f*_k]) + 2 eps (T_ab[f_k,f*_k] + T_ab[f*_k,f_k]) } = K_ab eps/(1+eps^2) (2 eps - sqrt2 cos(2 theta)). (2.16)' with (2.12)-(2.14) T[f,f] = -K e^{2i theta}, T[f*,f] = T[f,f*] = K, T[f*,f*] = -K e^{-2i theta}, theta = k_r x^r, K_ab = (k_a k_b - (1/2) eta_ab k_r k^r)/(2 omega L^3), = k_a k_b/(2 omega L^3) for massless. p.6: 'From Eq.(2.16), it follows that the condition for the expectation value of energy density to be negative is cos(2 theta) > sqrt2 eps.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free scalar field in FLAT spacetime (Minkowski), stress tensor as the bilinear form (2.11) T_mn[g,h] = d_m g d_n h - (1/2) eta_mn d_s g d^s h (minimal coupling, no mass term in (2.11))
H2 box normalisation, volume L^3, single plane-wave mode k, f_k = e^{i k.x}/sqrt(2 omega L^3) (implied by K_ab's 1/(2 omega L^3))
H3 massless for the simplified K_ab = k_a k_b/(2 omega L^3) (the general K_ab is also printed)
H4 normal ordering against the Minkowski vacuum: ':T_ab: = T_ab - <0|T_ab|0>' (p.4)
H5 state (2.15), superposition of |0> and the single-mode |2>, eps REAL 'for simplicity'
H6 the general-state expansion (2.10) in number eigenstates, from which (2.16)'s middle line is the c0,c2 specialisation

C1: (2.12)-(2.14) follow from (2.11) for f = e^{i k.x}/sqrt(2 omega L^3), massless, with K_ab as printed; K_00 = omega/(2L^3). C2/C3: <Psi|:T00:|Psi> from exact Fock matrices equals KF's own general-state formula (2.10) at c0 = 1/sqrt(1+eps^2), c2 = eps/sqrt(1+eps^2): rho = 2K eps(2eps - sqrt2 cos2th)/(1+eps^2). C4: the MIDDLE line equals it exactly; the FINAL line equals exactly half of it, identically in eps and theta. C5 (z3, with vacuity guard SAT): final == exact iff rho == 0. C6 (z3): sign(final) == sign(exact) everywhere, and rho < 0 iff cos2th > sqrt2 eps -- KF's stated negativity condition is exact and unaffected by the slip. C7: exact <:T00^2:> = 12K^2 eps^2/(1+eps^2); Delta with the exact rho = 1 - (2eps - sqrt2 cos2th)^2/(3(1+eps^2)) (reproduces the tree's witness 0.5134 at eps = 1/10, theta = 0); Delta with the final line would be 0.8784 there. C8 (context only, belongs to the (3.7)/(3.8) keys): KF (3.8) is reproduced by NONE of the four combinations {final, middle} x {printed (3.7), exact <:T00^2:>}, so the dropped 2 in (2.16) does not by itself explain (3.8).

later_literature.ref: B. Freivogel & D. Krommydas, 'The Smeared Null Energy Condition', arXiv:1807.03808
later_literature.what: Restates the vacuum-plus-two-particle class, attributing it to Kuo & Ford PRD 47 (1993) 4510 [their ref. 25], for |psi> = (sqrt3/2)|0_k> + (1/2)|2_k> in a continuum normalisation, and finds the smeared <T++> = (k/L)(1 - (sqrt3/2) cos(2x0.k) e^{-4 tau^2 k^2}) (their (24)): 'similar to that of [25], but due to the smearing the negative contribution ... is exponentially damped'. It does not print KF's single-mode coefficient, and a relative (constant : oscillating) coefficient CANNOT discriminate the factor 2, since KF's middle and final lines have the same relative coefficient and differ only overall. Their continuum convention was not reconciled with KF's box convention here.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence is the re-derivation itself: (2.16) is a closed-form Fock-space expectation value with NO empirical input -- no measured constant, no extrapolated datum. Everything needed (the canonical commutator, the box mode (2.12)-(2.14), the state (2.15)) was in Kuo & Ford's hands in 1993, and their own middle line and their own general formula (2.10) are both exact (C3, C4). The discrepancy is an algebra/transcription slip between two consecutive printed lines of v1 (a dropped overall 2), not a consequence of missing data. Having more data would change nothing. Evidence the other way -- that the slip matters: it does not move the sign of rho or the negativity condition cos2th > sqrt2 eps (z3 C6); it would halve rho and change any Delta built on it (C7), but (3.8) is not reproduced from either line (C8), so the slip is not the whole story of (3.8), which is a separate key. Whether PRD 47, 4510 carries the 2 is NAMED-NOT-READ.
